presentation: A 78-year-old man with history of hyperlipidemia, androgenetic alopecia, TIA, and osteopenia (on alendronate for the past year) presents because his dentist plans a tooth extraction with bone graft and implant. He is at high fracture risk due to his advanced age and weight, but no other FRAX risk factors. He is concerned about medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ). His only other medications are aspirin and atorvastatin. When should alendronate be held and resumed with respect to the procedure?
